changes.risk_reason: Removing references to the United States Regional Privacy Notice may reduce visibility into specific consumer privacy rights and how to exercise them.
changes.headline: Instagram removed references to its United States Regional Privacy Notice.
changes.what_changed: The policy no longer includes text pointing users to the United States Regional Privacy Notice for details on handling Personal Information and exercising privacy rights.
changes.what_it_means: US users may find it harder to locate specific information about their state-level privacy rights directly from this section of the policy.
changes.what_you_can_do: Look for the United States Regional Privacy Notice directly on Instagram's or Meta's privacy help pages to review your rights.
changes.before_excerpt:
Read the United States Regional Privacy Notice for more details about how we handle Personal Information and how to exercise your rights.
Privacy notice for United States residents
You can learn more about the consumer privacy rights that may be available to you by reviewing the United States Regional Privacy Notice.

changes.risk_reason: Removing references to the United States Regional Privacy Notice may reduce visibility into specific rights and options available to US residents.
changes.headline: Facebook removed mentions of its United States Regional Privacy Notice.
changes.what_changed: Facebook deleted text that pointed users to the United States Regional Privacy Notice for details on handling personal information and exercising privacy rights.
changes.what_it_means: Users may find it harder to locate specific information about US privacy rights and how to exercise them, since the direct references have been removed.
changes.what_you_can_do: Check Facebook's main Privacy Policy page directly for any US-specific privacy rights information, as the shortcut references have been removed.
changes.before_excerpt:

Privacy notice for United States residents

changes.risk_reason: This only adds a link to an existing regional notice explaining privacy rights, without changing data collection or sharing practices.
changes.headline: Instagram adds a pointer to its US Regional Privacy Notice for consumer rights.
changes.what_changed: Instagram added references and a link to a 'United States Regional Privacy Notice' that explains how it handles personal information and how US residents can exercise privacy rights.
changes.what_it_means: You now have an easier way to find information about your privacy rights as a US resident, such as rights to access or delete data, but no actual data practice appears to have changed.
changes.what_you_can_do: If you want to know your privacy rights, check the United States Regional Privacy Notice linked in Instagram's privacy policy.
changes.after_excerpt:
Read the United States Regional Privacy Notice for more details about how we handle Personal Information and how to exercise your rights.

changes.risk_reason: This adds a reference to an existing regional privacy notice explaining rights, without indicating new data collection or sharing.
changes.headline: Facebook adds a pointer to a US regional privacy notice explaining your rights.
changes.what_changed: Facebook added references and a link to a 'United States Regional Privacy Notice' that explains how it handles Personal Information and how US residents can exercise their privacy rights.
changes.what_it_means: This doesn't change what data Facebook collects or shares; it just makes it easier to find information about your legal privacy rights if you live in the US.
changes.what_you_can_do: If you want to know your privacy rights, check the new United States Regional Privacy Notice linked in Facebook's policy.
